title: A Novel Implementation Framework of Digital Twins for Intelligent Manufacturing Based on Container Technology and Cloud Manufacturing Services
authors: M. -H. Hung; Y. -C. Lin; H. -C. Hsiao; C. -C. Chen; K. -C. Lai; Y. -M. Hsieh; H. Tieng; T. -H. Tsai; H. -C. Huang; H. -C. Yang; F. -T. Cheng
source_title: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Many core technologies of Industry 4.0 have gained substantial advancement in recent years. Digital Twin (DT) has become the key technology and tool for manufacturing industries to realize intelligent cyber-physical integration and digital transformation by leveraging these technologies. Although there have been many DT-related works, there is no standard definition, unified framework, and implementation approach of DT until now. Widely developing DTs for the manufacturing industry is still challenging. Thus, this paper proposes a novel implementation framework of digital twins for intelligent manufacturing, denoted as IF-DTiM, which possesses several distinct merits to distinguish itself from previous works. First, IF-DTiM fully utilizes new-generation container technology so that DT-related applications and services can be packaged in a self-contained way, rapidly deployed, and robustly operated with the capabilities of failover, autoscaling, and load balancing. Second, it leverages existing intelligent cloud manufacturing services to realize the intelligence for DT externally in a scalable and plug-and-play manner instead of using traditional approaches to embed intelligence in DT. Third, IF-DTiM contains Product DT for products, Equipment DT (i.e., EQ DT) for equipment, and Process DT for production lines, which can generically fulfill the demands and scenarios to achieve intelligent manufacturing for various manufacturing industries. Testing results show that IF-DTiM can achieve remarkable performance in rapid deployment and real-time data exchanges of DT-related applications. Finally, we develop an example DTiM system for CNC machining based on IF-DTiM to demonstrate its efficacy and applicability in facilitating the manufacturing industry to build their DT systems. Note to Practitioners—Developing Digital Twin (DT) systems to realize intelligent manufacturing is challenging. The proposed IF-DTiM (Implementation Framework of Digital Twins for Intelligent Manufacturing) provides a novel container-technology and cloud-manufacturing-service-based systematic methodology for building DTiM. In this paper, we present the system architecture and several operational scenarios (e.g., how to create and use DTs) of IF-DTiM, together with the design of its core functional mechanisms (e.g., rapid deployment scheme for DT, real-time data exchange for DT, DT interface pattern, and general workflow architecture for DT). Also, an example DTiM system for CNC machining based on IF-DTiM is presented to facilitate the practitioners to adopt the designs and niches in IF-DTiM to build their desired DTiM systems.

title: Enhancing Fault Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks using Digital Twin and Predictive Maintenance
authors: S. Sharma; B. P. U. Ivy; M. Uppal; S. Mapari; D. Gupta; R. R
source_title: 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Smart Systems and Ubiquitous Computing (ICAUC)
abstract: The emergence of Wireless Sensor Networks has enabled the detection of potentially dangerous or catastrophic events prior to their actual occurrence. Wireless Sensor Networks rely on sensors that collect data on environmental conditions, allowing an early warning system to be implemented for potentially dangerous or catastrophic events, enabling an organization to take actions to prevent or mitigate these types of events. The technology digital twin has potential to improve ability of a wireless sensor network to detect faults and recover from them before the fault occurs. Digital Twins are real-time representations of physical objects or systems that track activity and behaviour of that physical object or system. By combining the Digital Twin with a Wireless Sensor Network, it is possible to create a model of predictive maintenance that can detect potential fault conditions before they occur by utilizing fault-analysis techniques. By utilizing this model to improve the Wireless Sensor Network, it is possible to improve the reliability and reduce the incidence of natural disasters. This report describes how Digital Twins can be created and how they can be used in Predictive Maintenance to increase the reliability of wireless sensor networks. These findings illustrate the power of such an AI-based approach toward completely transforming fault management within WSNs, toward being more robust, efficient, and reliable sensor networks in today's world.

title: Scalable Estimation of Functional Reserve in Technical Building Equipment Using Data-Driven and Physics-Informed Methods
authors: N. Ahmad; M. Kruettgen; J. Mueller
abstract: Technical Building Equipment (TBE), such as heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems, undergoes gradual performance degradation during operation that is not yet explicitly quantified by conventional indicators. Existing prognostic methods such as Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation generally depend on run-to-failure data or specialized sensing infrastructure that is rarely available in standard building automation systems. This paper introduces Functional Reserve (FR), a normalized asset-level performance indicator that quantifies the remaining performance margin between a component's current condition and its functional failure boundary on a 0–100% scale. To enable scalable deployment across heterogeneous building portfolios, a three-stage framework is proposed that combines automated asset discovery, component-specific Health Indicator computation, and a unified FR calculation. This modular design allows new component families to be incorporated by defining only the corresponding Health Indicator template, while keeping the remaining approach unchanged. The approach is demonstrated on a district heating heat exchanger in a museum in Cologne using 26 months of operational data. The framework is designed to be generic across TBE component families and produces a continuously updated metric, enabling building operators to prioritize maintenance across heterogeneous assets based on actual remaining performance margin rather than fixed time-based intervals.

title: Optimizing Industrial Ecosystem Demand Response Participation Using a Digital Twin
authors: E. Mityakov; A. Ladynin; A. Vuatkin
source_title: 2026 International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
abstract: Demand response (DR) programs offer industrial enterprises additional revenue but risk production disruptions and cascading output losses across cooperative supply chains. Existing DR optimization methods focus on single plants or micro grids, ignoring inter-firm material flows and technological constraints. This paper presents a digital-twin-based approach to optimizing industrial ecosystem DR participation. The digital twin simulates hourly load profiles, production plans, and cooperative ties for a 15-enterprise machine-building cluster. We formulate a multi-objective problem: maximizing DR revenue versus minimizing output losses. A random-search algorithm with heuristic correction and feasible-solution filtering generates 2000 candidate reduction schedules per scenario and constructs a Pareto front. We compare our method against uniform reduction (theoretical bound) and local independent optimization. Experiments on two operator-request scenarios (20% over 4 hours and 30% over 6 hours) show that our Pareto-compromise solution substantially outperforms local optimization: under the deeper scenario, net return improves by 41% and output losses drop by 20%, at equal operator revenue. However, the feasible-solution space narrows sharply under deep reduction-only 2 feasible schedules from 2000-indicating limited ecosystem flexibility. The digital twin enables cascading-effect modelling and data generation where real data are unavailable, making the approach applicable to new clusters. Future work includes adding tie preservation as an objective and calibrating on real data.

title: AI-Driven Predictive Maintenance in Industry 4.0: A Systematic Review and Research Directions
authors: H. Cherradi; K. Benjilali; A. Elasri; S. Hamida; B. Cherradi; O. Bouattane
source_title: 2026 6th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
abstract: Predictive maintenance (PdM) has emerged as a cornerstone of Industry 4.0, enabling data-driven decisionmaking to minimize downtime and optimize asset lifecycle management. Even though PdM tasks, such as anomaly detection and prescriptive maintenance, are increasingly using artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, the field is still fragmented across algorithms, evaluation procedures, and industrial contexts. In order to address this, we use VOSviewer to perform a systematic bibliometric analysis of 3.247 peer-reviewed publications from 2020 to 2025. The results show that there are four main research clusters: domain-specific applications, condition-based diagnostics, core AI methodologies, and Industry 4.0 infrastructure. Finally, we propose a unifying taxonomy in the Industry 4.0 stack that interconnects AI techniques to PdM applications, while also discussing the potential of explainability, human-AI cooperation and multitask learning as well as the crucial problems of generalizability, data-availability and lack of business justification. We believe this study provides a systematic architecture to equip scholars and practitioners with better insights to pursue the next step toward the building blocks of robust, interpretable and applicable PdM solutions.

title: Methodology for Designing Embedded Real-Time Electrothermal Models in PYNQ Z1 System on Chip
authors: J. M. Barón; A. Garcia; F. Vergara; P. J. Arnaiz; M. Vasić
abstract: This paper presents a design methodology for Real- Time Digital Twin Electrothermal Models on SoC (Systems on a Chip) developing an analysis of the most relevant constraints for Real-Time Operation and their classification. Moreover, the electrothermal model layout within the architecture of the PYNQ Z1 SoC will be presented exposing the advantages of using an external interface such as Jupyter for Forecasting and the role of parallel structures to accelerate the computation of numerical integration algorithms in Programmable Logic (PL). The proposed electrothermal models will be initially validated with simulation results and later compared with experimental data provided by CMCS (Compact Motor Control System), in which 4 asynchronous engines are supplied by 4 DC/AC IPBB (Inverter Power Building Block).

title: Cross-Modal Commonality Graph Matching Frame: A Fault Diagnosis Method for Multimode Process
authors: S. Tan; Z. Chen; Q. Jiang; W. Zhong
source_title: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Fault diagnosis in complex industrial systems, such as large-scale chemical plants and advanced manufacturing lines, is critically challenged by data acquired in multiple and varying operating modes. These modal shifts, driven by different production demands and process parameters, often obscure fault signatures and undermine the reliability of conventional diagnostic models. Despite these operational variations, it is observed that variables within such multimode processes often exhibit consistent correlations. Consequently, the same fault can manifest itself as a shared propagation characteristic across different modes. To leverage these invariant features for robust fault identification, this paper proposes a novel Cross-Modal Commonality Graph Matching (CMCGM) framework. Our approach first extracts the shared causal structures of a specific fault from data across multiple modalities to construct a modality-independent “commonality fault dictionary,” which captures the essential fault signature. By transforming the diagnosis task into a local subgraph matching problem against this dictionary, the CMCGM method achieves robust and accurate fault identification while circumventing the computational costs of online feature propagation. The effectiveness and superior performance of the proposed framework are validated through extensive experiments on the Tennessee-Eastman (TE) process, a widely-recognized benchmark for complex chemical systems. Note to Practitioners—This work addresses the challenge of diagnosing faults in industrial processes where data comes from multiple working modes. In such systems, faults often propagate in similar ways across different modalities, but traditional methods struggle to leverage these shared patterns effectively. Our solution, the Cross-Modal Commonality Graph Matching (CMCGM) framework, identifies and matches these common fault signatures across modalities, enabling faster and more reliable fault diagnosis without requiring extensive computational resources. The method works by analyzing how faults propagate across different data sources, extracting their shared structural features, and building a reusable fault reference library. Instead of treating each data stream separately, it compares faults in a way that reduces redundant computations. This makes the diagnosis process more efficient while maintaining reliability. One current limitation is that it requires sufficient historical fault records to build an effective reference model. Future improvements could focus on making the system more responsive to newly emerging faults and integrating it with real-time monitoring systems. Potential applications include predictive maintenance in factories, power plants, and other complex industrial systems where early and accurate fault detection is critical.

title: Towards a Digital Twin for Sustainable Asset Management of IoT Devices in Smart Buildings
authors: C. Okolo; N. Schmieder; M. Hellwig; E. Rigger
source_title: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Engineering, Technology, and Innovation (ICE/ITMC)
abstract: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in buildings holds immense potential for enhancing performance with respect to building efficiency or building sustainability. This paper systematically explores the literature in the intersection of IoT solutions, emerging digital technologies, sustainability, and Building Information Modelling. In this way, it sheds light on the state-of-the-art and the transformative potential of IoT and digital technologies in creating more sustainable buildings. While IoT systems are often used to improve various aspects of sustainability, the environmental sustainability of IoT systems themselves is rarely investigated. We therefore analyze the literature regarding the environmentally sustainable management of IoT devices employed. The analysis confirms a gap in the research in that IoT solutions are seen as a means to an end but are not the focus of sustainability considerations. Hence, it identifies the need for a sustainability-related Asset Management of IoT systems in buildings. It leads to the proposal of a corresponding implementation concept that bundles all the necessary IoT-related information of a building environment inside a Digital Twin. This establishes a comprehensive overview of the activities and properties of the IoT devices with applications in different use case scenarios, such as monitoring of operational states or insight into recycling potentials.

title: Robust Calibration of Vehicle Solid-State Lidar-Camera Perception System Using Line-Weighted Correspondences in Natural Environments
authors: S. Tang; Y. Feng; J. Huang; X. Li; Z. Lv; Y. Feng; W. Wang
source_title: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: With the rapid development of autonomous driving and SLAM technology, the perception system of a vehicle heavily relies on laser and image sensors to capture the real-world scenario and avoid obstacles autonomously. To achieve accurate and robust multi-sensor fusion computation, high-precision extrinsic calibration of camera and laser scanner is a necessary requirement. Traditional multi-sensor calibration methods based on manual features rely on specific scenarios and may not provide feature information over long distances. In this paper, we present a novel approach for robustly calibrating the extrinsic parameters of a solid-state(SS) lidar-camera system in a natural environment. Our proposed method begins with obtaining robust line feature information. we first innovatively employ a super-voxel clustering method to extract global 3D line features from the complete point cloud and then back-project these 3D line features into 2D space. Afterward, a transformer-based edge detection network, EDTER, is used to detect the edge features and estimate the probability pixel-by-pixel. To consider the uncertainty of two-dimensional line features and the inconsistency of residuals at different distances, we construct a line feature weight model for line feature residual calculation. Finally, we minimize the residual errors using least squares optimization to recover the relative pose of the camera and the lidar sensor. We conducted a performance study to compare our proposed method against existing targetless calibration methods on various natural scenarios. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves higher robustness, accuracy, and consistency, making it suitable for real-world applications.

title: Scheduling Under Uncertainty for Industry 4.0 and 5.0
authors: K. Bakon; T. Holczinger; Z. Süle; S. Jaskó; J. Abonyi
abstract: This article provides a review about how uncertainties in increasingly complex production and supply chains should be addressed in scheduling tasks. Uncertainty management will be particularly important in Industry 5.0 solutions that will require the close integration of operators and technical systems. To prepare for these challenging developments, this work reviews the sources of uncertainty and the scheduling algorithms that deal with the different types of models developed to handle the uncertain nature of the elements and the environment of complex technological systems. The paper not only identifies the challenges, but also the main building blocks that can help to manage and reduce uncertainties based on the I4.0 and I5.0 solutions. We hope that this study will serve as a starting point for R&D projects and algorithm developments, which will be needed primarily in the field of multi-agent, multistage and inverse optimizations.

title: From CAD to POMDP: Probabilistic Planning for Robotic Disassembly of End-of-Life Products
authors: J. Baumgärtner; M. Hansjosten; D. Hald; A. Hauptmannl; A. Puchta; J. Fleischer
source_title: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
abstract: To support the circular economy, robotic systems must not only assemble new products but also disassemble end-of-life (EOL) ones for reuse, recycling, or safe disposal. Existing approaches to disassembly sequence planning often assume deterministic and fully observable product models, yet real EOL products frequently deviate from their initial designs due to wear, corrosion, or undocumented repairs. We argue that disassembly should therefore be formulated as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), which naturally captures uncertainty about the product’s internal state. We present a mathematical formulation of disassembly as a POMDP, in which hidden variables represent uncertain structural or physical properties. Building on this formulation, we propose a task and motion planning framework that automatically derives specific POMDP models from CAD data, robot capabilities, and inspection results. To obtain tractable policies, we approximate this formulation with a reinforcement-learning approach that operates on stochastic action outcomes informed by inspection priors, while a Bayesian filter continuously maintains beliefs over latent EOL conditions during execution. Using three products on two robotic systems, we demonstrate that this probabilistic planning framework outperforms deterministic baselines in terms of average disassembly time and variance, generalizes across different robot setups, and successfully adapts to deviations from the CAD model, such as missing or stuck parts.

title: Building a Resilient and Robust Supply Chain with Enhanced Resistance
authors: S. L. dos Santos Alvim; E. M. Frazzon; E. R. da Silva; A. F. de Oliveira; R. F. Castro; D. de Simas
source_title: 2025 16th IEEE International Conference on Industry Applications (INDUSCON)
abstract: In an era marked by uncertainty and disruption, supply chain (SC) resilience and robustness have become strategic imperatives. This study introduces the Supply Chain Resistance Index (SCRESIS Index), which was developed employing simulation methods. Digital Twin and artificial neural network technologies are conceptually discussed as potential enablers for future applications; however, they are not implemented in this study. The proposed framework enhances adaptability and stability by integrating resilience and robustness. The results demonstrate that combining rapid adaptation with structural resistance provides a competitive advantage in volatile environments.

title: Digital Twin for DCs: a Reference Architecture Based On BIM, IoT and Analytics Control
authors: S. Meschini; P. Gasbarri; L. C. Tagliabue; V. Vaccaro; R. Birke; M. Aldinucci
source_title: 2026 34th Euromicro International Conference on Parallel, Distributed, and Network-Based Processing (PDP)
abstract: Data centers (DCs) represent one of the most energy-intensive and operationally critical categories of buildings, supporting essential digital services such as cloud computing, large-scale data storage, and artificial intelligence applications. Their operation is characterized by complex interdependencies between information technology loads, cooling infrastructures, power distribution systems, and environmental conditions. Ensuring efficiency, reliability, and resilience under these constraints remains a significant challenge for operators and designers alike. In recent years, the concept of Digital Twin (DT) has emerged as a promising paradigm to address this complexity by enabling a continuously updated digital representation of physical systems, enriched with real-time data and analytical capabilities. Despite increasing attention in both academia and industry, DT solutions for buildings and DCs remain largely fragmented. Existing approaches often focus on individual aspects such as visualization, simulation, or monitoring dashboards, while failing to provide robust integration between design data, operational measurements, and control systems. A recurring limitation concerns the lack of interoperability between Building Information Modeling (BIM) data and Internet of Things (IoT) infrastructures, which prevents the construction of coherent and scalable DT systems. This paper proposes a reference architecture for DT applied to DCs, grounded in the integration of BIM-based representations, real-time IoT data acquisition, analytical models, and control mechanisms. The architecture adopts a layered perspective, separating concerns related to data management, semantic integration, modeling, analytics, and actuation, while maintaining consistency across these layers. Informed by recent reviews on building-scale DT, the proposed approach addresses the well-known bottlenecks associated with BIM usage and data acquisition. The contribution of this work lies in providing an architectural blueprint able to support interoperability and reuse, offering a structured foundation for the development of advanced DT solutions in DC environments, and complemented by practical metrics that make DT implementations assessable beyond project-specific prototypes.

title: Intelligent Optimization of Manufacturing Supply Chains via Digital Twins and Deep Learning
authors: S. Ma; J. Qian
source_title: 2025 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Electrical, Automation and Computer Engineering (ICEACE)
abstract: Against the backdrop of volatile markets, this paper examines the collaborative optimization path of “perception-prediction-decision-feedback” within the manufacturing enterprise supply chain. This paper establishes an intelligent optimization system based on digital twins: IoT data is combined with a simulation core to create synchronized virtual and physical counterparts (Twin). Time series deep learning models (ARIMA, LSTM/optional TFT) are used to predict and analyze demand and inventory. Multi-objective intelligent optimization methods (improved particle swarm and ant colony algorithms) and robustness evaluation methods (FCE and Monte Carlo methods) are employed to achieve a closedloop decision-making process. The supply chain is transformed into a graphical model that reflects time changes, and a graph neural network (GNN) is implemented to measure the edge weights of the transportation network. The dynamic road conditions are combined with the order status to improve the path decision-making level. The public data of fresh food logistics in 2023 is analyzed and a simulation platform is built. The results show that the average delivery time is reduced by about 2.1 days, the on-time delivery rate of orders is increased by more than 12 percentage points, and the cost is reduced by nearly 20 percentage points. Even in the event of multiple interferences, self-recovery can be achieved within 8 hours. The combination of Twin+DL+dynamic optimization has effectively promoted the improvement of supply chain prediction accuracy, the strengthening of global collaboration and the enhancement of robustness, providing a replicable technical approach for the intelligent upgrade of the manufacturing industry.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Circular Economy Transformation: System Design Insights from Emerging Applications
authors: T. Alsaoudi; E. Ouda; A. Acquaye; M. Khalfan
source_title: 2025 International Conference on INnovations in Intelligent SysTems and Applications (INISTA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive systematic literature review (SLR) investigating the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in advancing Circular Economy (CE) practices across diverse industries from 2015 to 2025. Starting with an initial dataset of 815 articles retrieved exclusively from the Scopus database, a systematic screening process based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria reduced the collection to 335 studies. Following a thorough quality evaluation and relevance assessment, a final sample of 49 articles was selected for analysis. The review encompasses a diverse range of application domains, including manufacturing, waste management, energy systems, and supply chains. It further identifies the targeted CE strategies enabled by these AI applications, such as resource optimization, waste reduction, product life extension, and emission mitigation. Building upon this synthesis, the study proposes a robust conceptual framework designed to facilitate the strategic integration of AI technologies within CE initiatives. Based on the analysis of the final sample of 49 papers, the proposed framework offers actionable design implications. It identifies critical innovation pathways to support the development of intelligent and sustainable CE solutions. By combining theoretical foundations with empirical evidence, this research advances AI-enabled sustainability and promotes the development of intelligent systems for sustainable circular transformation.

title: A Review of current practices and challenges in Green Data Centers: renewable energy sources, waste heat recovery, and intelligent management systems
authors: M. Boscariol; E. Cacciaguerra; P. Gasbarri; D. Accardo; S. Meschini; L. C. Tagliabue
source_title: 2025 33rd Euromicro International Conference on Parallel, Distributed, and Network-Based Processing (PDP)
abstract: As digital transformation advances, Data Centers are crucial in supporting global digital infrastructure but contribute substantially to energy consumption and carbon emissions. Green Data Center technologies emerged to address such sustainability challenges, integrating energy-efficient designs, renewable energy, and waste heat recovery solutions. The review explores advancements in sustainable Data Centers, focusing on Building Information Modelling (BIM), Digital Twins (DTs), and intelligent management systems, that help mitigating environmental impacts. BIM and DTs support realtime monitoring, predictive analysis, and optimized energy management, helping operators minimize cooling needs, reduce inefficiencies, and maximize renewable energy use.The interest in renewable energy sources such as solar power is increasing, highlighting hydrogen fuel cells potential in providing a scalable, low-emission alternative to conventional backup power. Waste heat recovery also plays a crucial role in Green Data Centers, with initiatives repurposing heat for district heating, industrial processes, and building heating. Current applications include Data Centers where heat recovery systems supply residential heating, support algae farms, and enhance university campus efficiency.Beyond energy efficiency, Green Data Centers contribute to smart grid stability. Load-shifting capabilities enable power usage to be adjusted during peak and off-peak times, enhancing grid resilience and promoting sustainability. Future trends include AI-driven resource management, further carbon footprint reduction via green energy procurement, and advanced load distribution strategies.The review synthesizes current research and practices, showcasing sustainable technologies in Green Data Centers, presenting case studies of successful implementations. It also highlights promising applications and existing challenges in achieving carbon-neutral infrastructures.

title: A Hybrid Multi-Agent Architecture for Resilient Logistics Planning Under Demand and Supply Uncertainty
authors: A. Akhmet-Sultan
source_title: 2026 IEEE 6th International Conference on Smart Information Systems and Technologies (SIST)
abstract: Modern supply chains operate under volatile demand and frequent disruptions, demanding planning systems that are both locally adaptive and globally coordinated. Traditional multi-agent system (MAS) architectures for logistics struggle to balance this trade-off, creating a significant governance gap in autonomous decision-making. This paper proposes a novel hybrid MAS architecture formally grounded in the subsidiarity principle to address this gap. The architecture is structured around a three-level governance model (operation, tactical, strategic) with specialized agents, formalized interactions using Foundation for Intelligent Physical Agents (FIPA) protocols, and a shared Web Ontology Language (OWL) ontology for semantic interoperability. Its adaptive behaviour is realized through an integrated suite of risk-aware algorithms distributed across all levels, enabling balanced decisionmaking from real-time reaction to long-term strategic evolution. The paper further contributes a comprehensive experimental design for validation, defining canonical baseline models (centralized and decentralized) and key performance indicators (KPIs) for simulation-based comparison. Together, these components provide a coherent framework for resilient logistics planning. The work contributes both a principled blueprint for building intelligent supply chain systems and a rigorous methodology for their empirical evaluation.

title: Real-Time Adaptive Gray-Box Digital Twin for Industrial Equipment: Online Calibration and Edge-Deployable Prediction
authors: X. Wen; C. Wen
source_title: 2026 11th International Symposium on Advances in Electrical, Electronics and Computer Engineering (ISAEECE)
abstract: Industrial assets frequently experience parameter drift during operation, which degrades predictive models and inflates maintenance costs. Because purely data-driven models struggle with covariate shift and physics-based models accumulate approximation biases, this paper proposes a Minimal Gray-Box Digital Twin for real-time condition monitoring and adaptive state prediction in embedded systems. The architecture integrates an interpretable state-space backbone, an online Extended Kalman Filter and Recursive Least Squares layer for training-free parameter tracking, and a lightweight residual neural network to capture unmodeled nonlinearities, structurally guided by a threeterm error decomposition strategy. Validated across three physical simulation benchmarks and a real-world building energy dataset, the proposed method yields statistically significant performance gains with a p-value less than 0.01. Crucially, the model achieves a rapid recovery of 20 plus or minus 19 steps and an ultra-low latency of 54.6 microseconds per step on an edge-class CPU. Utilizing merely 4500 neural parameters and approximately 2 megabytes of memory, the proposed framework presents a highly efficient, embedded-ready alternative to computationally demanding Physics-Informed Neural Networks and deep learning approaches that rely on runtime gradient updates.

title: Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning for Secure Cloud Scheduling with Digital Twin Validation
authors: N. N. Gadani; R. Anjaria
source_title: 2025 14th International Conference on Renewable Energy Research and Applications (ICRERA)
abstract: Cloud-based time-critical smart grid applications need to be able to efficiently schedule resources to maintain their performance and robustness in the presence of time varying loads and cyber intrusions. In fact, we find that simple heuristics as Round-Robin (RR) and Least-Loaded (LL) are not viable choices in adversarial settings and that single-layer DRL architectures cannot scale well and are not stable. To enable attack-aware and efficient performance scheduling, this work introduces a Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning (HDRL) based structure along with a digital twin (DT) validation environment. In the HDRL model, local and global PPO agents work in sync to allocate resources at various levels and DT orchestrates redundancy of workloads and cyberattacks injection for resilience purposes. The assessment was performed on actual building load traces with normal, low attack, and high attack profiles. The results indicate that HDRL outperforms the baselines in terms of throughput, SLA violations and recovery time. Under high attack, HDRL also exhibited a reduction in SLA violations of more than 50% relative to LL and RR as well as $50 \%$ decrease in the time needed for recovery. Using Wilcoxon signed-rank test, we statistically validate that the improvements by HDRL are indeed significant with adversarial workloads. These results conclude HDRL with DT validation to be a novel and viable approach to secure, resilient, and flexible scheduling in the cloud for smart grid applications.

title: HAPS-Enabled Downlink Coverage Enhancement in Islands and Maritime Areas
authors: H. Lin; M. A. Kishk; M. -S. Alouini
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) are poised to play a critical role in next-generation mobile communications, offering enhanced flexibility, improved line-of-sight (LoS) conditions, and overcoming the limitations of terrestrial networks (TNs). Among NTN platforms, high altitude platform stations (HAPSs) have emerged as a promising solution to provide Internet connectivity to underserved regions, including rural areas, islands, and maritime zones, where traditional infrastructure deployment is costly and challenging to deploy. In this paper, we investigate the feasibility of large-scale HAPS deployment to connect island and maritime users, considering real-world shadowing effects on part of HAPSs caused by the presence of island building clusters. We first analyze the coverage performance of onshore (island) and offshore (remote sea) users, in which the channels between HAPSs and the user follow the shadowed Rician distributions and Rician distributions, respectively. Next, we introduce an evaluation method for nearshore users in a hybrid channel environment with HAPSs, and propose approximations that can reduce computational complexity. Based on the simulation results, we discuss how the distance from the island boundary (i.e. the relative remoteness of maritime users) affects coverage performance under different HAPS densities. We also emphasize the importance of choosing a balanced HAPS density or an advanced HAPS deployment scheme.

title: Integrating Blockchain, SSI, and RBAC for the Secure Management of Defense Heritage Buildings
authors: G. Baralla; L. Cocco; M. Di Francesco; R. Tonelli
abstract: This paper presents a Blockchain-SSI based system designed for the management and monitoring of historical heritage, with a focus on Italian defence heritage buildings. The system supports a modular architecture to integrate cutting-edge technologies, including decentralized applications managed through Smart Contracts and SSI, to enhance security, data integrity, and user autonomy in personal data management. Central to our system is the innovative dual-layer access control that combines SSI with Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), ensuring decentralized and secure management of identities and access permissions. A key component of the building system’s architecture is the blockchain module that enables the certification of data, documents or activities while offering query and verification services on this certified data. Through a detailed exploration of use-case scenarios, this paper illustrates the practical application and benefits of the system, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize heritage conservation practices. The use of Blockchain technology in this context represents an exceptional opportunity for data integrity and reliability among stakeholders, securing and tracing maintenance and processes in historic defence buildings. Additionally, the mechanism for access level control by integrating SSI and RBAC provides robust management of the system while simultaneously empowering individuals to retain control over their data.

title: V2LLM: A Digital-Twin-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model for Resilient Telemetry Recovery and Fault Diagnosis in V2X
authors: B. Hazarika; K. Singh; N. -S. Vo; B. Canberk; S. L. Cotton; H. Shin; T. Q. Duong
source_title: IEEE Transactions on Network Science and Engineering
abstract: Reliable telemetry is essential for fault detection and adaptive control in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) networks, yet wireless impairments often cause bursty, non-i.i.d. data loss. This paper proposes V2LLM, a digital-twin-aware, retrieval-augmented large language model (LLM) framework for resilient telemetry recovery and continual fault diagnosis. Leveraging the reasoning capabilities of large AI models (LAMs), V2LLM performs token-efficient reconstruction by combining local history, memory-guided context, and digital twin predictions. A sliding-window autoregressive scheme enables structured recovery under long gaps, while a federated continual learning module adapts fault classifiers at roadside units without raw data sharing. V2LLM tightly integrates semantic prompting, predictive modeling, and distributed adaptation to address uncertainty, heterogeneity, and spatiotemporal drift in V2X environments. Extensive evaluations show that the proposed framework consistently improves reconstruction quality and classification robustness, demonstrating the potential of LAM-powered architectures for intelligent, resilient wireless systems.

title: Evolution, Assessment and Extrapolation of National Training Strategies for a Decarbonized Building Stock
authors: L. Stojanovska-Georgievska; J. Cromwijk; G. Callinan; I. F. Sandeva; A. Krleski
source_title: 2026 11th International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Technologies (SpliTech)
abstract: Buildings remain responsible for around 40% of final energy use and over one-third of energy-related greenhouse gas emissions in the European Union, making the skills of the construction workforce a critical enabler for implementing EPBD IV, EED and RED targets. Since 2011, the BUILD UP Skills initiative has supported the development of national skills roadmaps for the building sector across 30 EU countries, originally under the Intelligent Energy Europe programme (2012-2013) and more recently through LIFE Clean Energy Transition (LIFE CET) projects that update and extend these roadmaps to 2030. This paper presents a comparative analysis of first-generation (2012-2013) and updated (2021-2024) national skills roadmaps from 15 European countries, develops a harmonized evaluation framework to identify evolution patterns, and derives a consolidated EU BUILD UP Skills roadmap structure. Using structured document analysis combined with SWOT-based assessment, we extract evolution factors (e.g., training volume expansion ratios, target-group diversification, skill-area broadening) that characterize the transition from 2020-oriented to 2030 -oriented roadmaps. These patterns enable an extrapolation method to project 2030 training needs for countries without updated roadmaps. Results show that updated roadmaps increase training volumes by factors ranging from 1.4 to 2.8, systematically broaden coverage to white-collar professionals, and integrate digital, circular-economy and system-integration competencies. The paper outlines key elements of a consolidated EU roadmap and demonstrates how extrapolation can fast-track skills planning in countries lagging behind, supporting the large-scale deployment of advanced retrofit solutions under the new EU policy framework.

title: The Role of Standards in The Environmental Digital Twins Architectures
authors: P. Zaborowski; B. L. Bye; A. J. Berre; R. Atkinson; A. Villar; M. -F. Voidrot; R. Palma
source_title: IGARSS 2024 - 2024 IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) can be considered as the next level of environmental analytics systems, providing environments to leverage research simulations within operational contexts. Integrating research and operational data acquisition, models, and simulations DT creates additional heterogeneity in the control mechanisms and outcomes (including quality, trust, and determinism) on top of the well-known data interoperability challenges. Interoperability is also evolving to encompass issues of reuse at scale with new technologies and ecosystem capabilities like cloud, HP/Quantum Computing, Machine Learning, AI, and various data sources, including airborne, drones, and in situ data. Interoperability is also time-sensitive, constrained by commonly used software solutions and their integration, and challenged by new requirements and technologies. Standards Development Organisations underpin interoperability standards over longer periods, whereas community-driven efforts continually define conventions, good practices, and reusable templates. These evolve faster and deeper into the domains than standards and common implementation technologies.Based on the OGC Standards Program, OGC Test Beds working on the Datacubes, Analysis Ready Data, Agile Reference Architecture and Transfer Machine Learning, and Iliad projects, authors present recent achievements and needs for transparent and scalable interoperability corresponding to various levels of common sense and new areas, where parallel interoperability spaces can co-exist as infrastructures evolve and interconnected across multiple domains.

title: Merging Model-Based and Data-Driven Approaches for Resilient Systems Digital Twins Design
authors: L. Campanile; M. S. de Biase; R. De Fazio; M. Di Giovanni; F. Marulli; L. Verde
source_title: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Cyber Security and Resilience (CSR)
abstract: Nowadays, the problem of system robustness, es-pecially in critical infrastructures, is a challenging open question. Some systems provide crucial services continuously failing, threatening the availability of the provided services. By designing a robust architecture, this criticality could be overcome or limited, ensuring service continuity. The definition of a resilient system involves not only its architecture but also the methodology implemented for the calculation and analysis of some indices, quantifying system performance. This study provides an innovative architecture for Digital Twins implementation based on a hybrid methodology for improving the control system in realtime. The introduced approach brings together different techniques. In particular, the work combines the point of strengths of Model-based methods and Data-driven ones, aiming to improve system performances.

title: Enhancing Fault Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks using Digital Twin and Predictive Maintenance
authors: S. Sharma; B. P. U. Ivy; M. Uppal; S. Mapari; D. Gupta; R. R
source_title: 2026 International Conference on AI-Driven Smart Systems and Ubiquitous Computing (ICAUC)
abstract: The emergence of Wireless Sensor Networks has enabled the detection of potentially dangerous or catastrophic events prior to their actual occurrence. Wireless Sensor Networks rely on sensors that collect data on environmental conditions, allowing an early warning system to be implemented for potentially dangerous or catastrophic events, enabling an organization to take actions to prevent or mitigate these types of events. The technology digital twin has potential to improve ability of a wireless sensor network to detect faults and recover from them before the fault occurs. Digital Twins are real-time representations of physical objects or systems that track activity and behaviour of that physical object or system. By combining the Digital Twin with a Wireless Sensor Network, it is possible to create a model of predictive maintenance that can detect potential fault conditions before they occur by utilizing fault-analysis techniques. By utilizing this model to improve the Wireless Sensor Network, it is possible to improve the reliability and reduce the incidence of natural disasters. This report describes how Digital Twins can be created and how they can be used in Predictive Maintenance to increase the reliability of wireless sensor networks. These findings illustrate the power of such an AI-based approach toward completely transforming fault management within WSNs, toward being more robust, efficient, and reliable sensor networks in today's world.

title: Research on Intelligent Fault Diagnosis and Self-Healing Control for Smart Grids Based on Digital Twin
authors: L. Guo; H. Hu; F. Chen
source_title: 2025 7th International Conference on Energy Systems and Electrical Power (ICESEP)
abstract: As the structure of smart grids becomes increasingly complex, traditional fault handling methods face severe challenges in response speed and decision optimization. To address this issue, this paper proposes and constructs a framework for smart grid fault diagnosis and self-healing control based on digital twin technology. The core of this framework is a co-simulation-based multi-scale hybrid modeling method: an Electromagnetic Transient (EMT) model built with MATLAB/Simulink is capable of generating high-fidelity data, while an Electromechanical Transient (RMS) model developed in OpenDSS serves as a "decision-making sandbox" for the rapid deduction of multi-agent self-healing strategies. This study introduces a novel validation methodology where the digital twin is used to generate data for complex fault scenarios—such as high-impedance faults—that are poorly represented in standard datasets. Our CNN-LSTM fault diagnosis model, when augmented with this twin-generated data, demonstrates significantly improved robustness. In terms of fault diagnosis, the CNN-LSTM model designed in this study achieved an accuracy of 99.5% on a public benchmark dataset, with an average diagnosis time of only 26.1ms, striking a superior balance between performance and efficiency compared to other advanced algorithms. Building on this, the twin-inferred self-healing control strategy can complete fault isolation and restoration decisions within 2 seconds, increasing the system load recovery rate from 70% with traditional methods to 95% in typical scenarios. In summary, the digital twin framework proposed in this study provides an effective technical solution for the rapid and precise handling of grid faults, demonstrating its application potential in building future autonomous power systems.

title: Integrating Intelligent Fault Recovery Mechanisms into Real-Time System Software for Resilient Embedded Application Design
authors: K. Santhosh; E. Boddepalli; S. G; V. Waiker; S. Thawkar; A. Balakumar
source_title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Trends in Engineering Systems and Technologies (ICTEST)
abstract: Embedded systems used in real-time applications-such as aerospace, healthcare, and industrial automation-must operate continuously and reliably, even in the presence of unexpected faults. Traditional fault-tolerance techniques, such as watchdog timers, static redundancy, and checkpoint/restart methods, often suffer from delayed recovery, high resource consumption, and limited adaptability to dynamic fault conditions. These limitations hinder the resilience and real-time performance of embedded systems, especially in complex and resource-constrained environments. This research proposes an intelligent fault recovery framework that integrates adaptive machine learning-based fault detection and autonomous recovery mechanisms directly into real-time system software. The methodology involves collecting fault data from testbeds and fault injection tools, training predictive models using decision trees and LSTM networks, and embedding these models into the real-time operating system (RTOS). Reinforcement learning is employed to optimize recovery actions dynamically based on system state and context. The system was evaluated through controlled experiments involving synthetic and real-world fault scenarios. Results demonstrate significant improvements in fault detection accuracy, reduced recovery latency, and minimal deadline violations compared to conventional methods. The proposed approach enhances system resilience without compromising real-time constraints, offering a robust solution for building self-healing embedded systems capable of intelligent fault management in critical applications.

title: Automated Progress Monitoring of Power Infrastructure Construction via YOLOv8 Detection, Iterative Closest Point Alignment, and BIM Integration
authors: Y. Xiao
source_title: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Electronics, Energy Systems and Power Engineering (EESPE)
abstract: Accurate and timely progress monitoring of power infrastructure construction sites, including substations, wind turbine foundations, photovoltaic mounting arrays, and transmission tower assemblies, is essential for grid commissioning schedules and for safety critical quality control. Traditional manual inspection is slow, costly, and subjective. This work presents a computer vision and Building Information Modeling integration framework that replaces fully image based three dimensional reconstruction with a feature level pipeline of YOLOv8 detection, structure from motion keypoint recovery, and Iterative Closest Point registration to the BIM reference model. The iterative optimization of the rigid transform is formulated explicitly, and geometric and temporal deviation metrics are defined with associated confidence intervals. Experiments are conducted on a multi site dataset of 15,360 labeled images collected from a 220 kV substation, an onshore wind farm, and a 50 MW photovoltaic plant, with controlled diversity in lighting, occlusion, and viewpoint. The proposed pipeline attains a mean average precision at intersection over union 0.5 of 0.942, an average alignment error of 17.6 mm, and a project level schedule deviation index of 2.9 percent. A paired comparison against Mask R CNN, Faster R CNN, and SSD baselines shows statistically significant gains at the 0.01 level. Relative to manual inspection, the pipeline reduces daily labor from 180 to 45 minutes per site and reduces absolute deviation error from 6.5 percent to 2.9 percent. The framework targets digital twin integration of energy infrastructure and supports smart grid commissioning workflows.

title: Scan-to-QC: Quality Control of Prefabricated Structural Systems Using Point Clouds
authors: R. Maalek; S. Maalek
abstract: Background: The use of point clouds to perform quality control (QC) of prefabricated structural systems is growing markedly. The sustained application of point clouds on construction projects at scale, however, requires reliable and automated frameworks to foster practicality. Literature Review: Existing solutions seldom incorporate the impact of instrument artifacts, construction errors, and complex element geometries, rendering the frameworks error-prone and sensitive to thresholds, outliers, and missing data. More specifically, current methods: 1) are not generalizable to any freeform element; 2) rely on local primitives, which increases runtime and threshold subjectivity; 3) do not formulate the point cloud to model fitting based on geometric distance; and 4) do not incorporate a dedicated outlier detection to explicitly handle large outliers. Methodology: This study presents, scan-to-QC, a generic solution for automatic QC of prefabricated elements with non-analytic cross-sections using point clouds. The framework addresses the current state-of-the-art limitations (above) by providing a generic, direct artificial-intelligence (AI)-based geometric distance fitting robust to outliers. The proposed approach introduces four new algorithms to: 1) represent the cross-sectional boundaries of elements with trigonometric polynomials, 2) perform orthogonal fitting of points to these polynomials, 3) remove outlying observations through robust concentration steps (CS), and 4) perform assembly verification of prefabricated elements in construction projects. As the convergence of CS depends on the initial fitting parameters, the performances of seven deterministic, heuristic, and AI-based (i.e., metaheuristic and global computational intelligence-based) optimization strategies to recover these parameters were evaluated on point clouds of five common prefabricated elements with complex geometries. The comparative analysis considered factors such as the fit quality, object detection accuracy, and computation runtime. Results and Conclusions: Among these methods, the Particle Swarm (PS) achieved the best results, significantly outperforming Simulated Annealing, Bayesian, and Genetic Algorithm. Furthermore, by fine-tuning the swarm size, the PS attained 99% and 96% accuracies in object detection and fitting quality, respectively. Finally, the calibrated PS algorithm was applied to the point cloud of a real-world prefabricated spaceframe structure, yielding 98.5% reliability in nodal coordinate estimation compared to the ground truth.

title: Interpretable Optimization-Inspired Deep Network for Off-Grid Frequency Estimation
authors: P. Pan; Y. Zhang; Y. Li; Y. Ye; W. He; Y. Zhu; R. Guo
source_title: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
abstract: The accuracy of on-grid frequency estimation methods suffers from the quantization error of discrete grids. In this article, a deep unfolded network for off-grid frequency estimation is proposed, dubbed OGFreq. In the OGFreq, there exist two kinds of variables. One is the batch-oriented dictionary for frequency-domain transform, and the other one is the instance-specific on-grid frequency and off-grid bias. As the dictionary is required to be universally applicable among all observed signals, network layers are designed and network weights are updated to approximate the transform bases in a data-driven way. Besides, instance-specific on-grid frequencies and off-grid biases are solved by unfolding the iterative soft-threshold algorithm (ISTA). In addition, the instance-specific hyperparameters for sparsity in ISTA are obtained by an encoder-decoder soft-threshold (EDS) module with the attention mechanism. In this way, the dictionary, on-grid frequency, and off-grid bias are learned in a unified data-driven framework. Numerical experiments show that the OGFreq obtains 4% lower false negative rate (FNR) when the SNR is 20 dB. Moreover, the computational complexity is one order of magnitude lower than the iteration-based off-grid frequency estimation methods. Finally, the robustness of the OGFreq is discussed when extended to the impulse noise and damped signals.

title: Security-Aware Geometrically Robust 3D Watermarking: Threat Models, Games, and Evaluation Protocols
authors: J. Djumanov; T. Khudayberganov; Z. Ibrohimova; R. Raxmanov; J. Uralov; E. Umarov
source_title: 2026 IEEE 27th International Conference of Young Professionals in Electron Devices and Materials (EDM)
abstract: Geometrically robust 3D watermarking is a practical mechanism for protecting digital graphical assets used in CAD/CAM, entertainment pipelines, digital twins, and additive manufacturing. However, many works still equate “robustness” with survival under routine processing (e.g., smoothing or decimation) and rarely specify what an adaptive adversary can observe, query, or optimize. Building on a review of spectral-geometric invariants under realistic 3D acquisition distortions, this paper proposes a security-aware blueprint for evaluating and designing robust 3D watermarks under explicit threat assumptions. We contribute three methodological layers. First, we formalize a threat model capturing representation changes (mesh ↔ point cloud), acquisition-reconstruction loops, oracle access to embedding or detection services, collusion across many samples, and a utility constraint that prevents trivial “removal by destruction.” Second, we introduce gamebased security definitions for removal, forgery, ambiguity, payload manipulation, and key recovery, with measurable adversarial advantages at a fixed detector operating point (controlled false-alarm rate). Third, we propose a parameterized attack taxonomy and a reproducible attacklibrary interface supporting composed attacks, adaptive score minimization, and standardized metadata logging. The resulting protocol reports both robustness curves (TPR/BER vs. attack strength) and security curves (e.g., key-recovery advantage vs. the number of observed assets). We illustrate the blueprint on spectral-geometric invariant watermarking, highlighting eigenbasis drift under remeshing/reconstruction and key-leakage risks under key reuse.

title: Systems Engineering Flexibility for Complex Adaptive Systems: Broadening the Concept of System Engineering
authors: P. De Haan; A. James; M. Efatmaneshnik; S. Lee
abstract: System Engineering has been integral to some of mankind’s greatest achievements in the 20th Century from launching astronauts into space to building some of the most intricately designed and built systems ever devised. However large-scale systems acquisition has often struggled conceptually with being responsive to change. Often this stems from engineering following a defined process focused on solving the challenges presented to them and devising an end-product(s) that meets specifications. This paper draws parallels from the challenges faced by businesses to stay relevant in a forever-changing dynamic business environment to glean lessons for defence acquisition. We suggest exploring circular systems engineering ecosystems to address the needs of stakeholders seeking to create future-proof complex adaptive systems and products that must operate in uncertain environments. The main goals here are to address the inherent uncertainty and improve stakeholder value.

This Industrial IoT book follows the journey of data from the shop floor to the boardroom, identifying goals and aiding in strong architectural decision-making. You’ll begin from the ground up, analyzing environment needs and understanding what is required from the captured data, applying industry standards and conventions throughout the process. This will help you realize why digital integration is crucial and how to approach an Industrial IoT project from a holistic perspective. As you advance, you’ll delve into the operational technology realm and consider integration patterns with common industrial protocols for data gathering and analysis with direct connectivity to data through sensors or systems. The book will equip you with the essentials for designing industrial IoT architectures while also covering intelligence at the edge and creating a greater awareness of the role of machine learning and artificial intelligence in overcoming architectural challenges. title: Digital Triplet-Enabled Regenerative Planning for Climate-Resilient Heritage City Centers: A Case Study of Alun-Alun Bandung, Indonesia
authors: M. Savitri; R. Sulaiman
source_title: 2026 13th International Conference on ICT for Smart Society (ICISS)
abstract: Historic city centers in rapidly growing cities face interconnected challenges of climate vulnerability, development pressure, congestion, environmental decline, and heritage degradation. In Bandung, Indonesia, Alun-Alun Bandung is a strategic urban core where civic identity, religious activity, commerce, public space, and colonial-era heritage intersect, while also facing flooding, limited green open space, traffic pressure, heat island effects, and fragmented heritage management. This paper proposes a Digital Triplet-enabled regenerative planning framework for climate-resilient heritage city centers, using Alun-Alun Bandung as an embedded case study. The framework integrates Nature-Based Solutions (NBS), Transfer of Development Rights (TDR), and climate-responsive adaptive reuse of heritage buildings. Methodologically, the study applies a qualitative embedded case study supported by spatial observation, policy review, project-based urban design data, and scenario-based indicator assessment. The Digital Triplet is structured through physical, digital, and socio-governance layers, linking existing urban conditions, analytical modeling, and planning decision-making. Preliminary assessment indicates that NBS improves ecological performance, TDR supports conservation financing and development control, and adaptive reuse reduces demolition-related carbon impacts while strengthening historical identity. The study contributes to smart city and regenerative urbanism discourse by positioning Digital Triplet as a governance-oriented decision-support framework for heritage-sensitive climate adaptation in the Global South

abstract: Data-driven discovery of governing equations from spatiotemporal observations is a key step toward interpretable and transferable models of controlled dynamical systems. Existing methods face a fundamental trade-off: sparse-regression methods such as SINDy depend on predefined libraries and may miss localized or control-coupled mechanisms, whereas prior-free symbolic regression explores large expression spaces with limited use of domain knowledge. Our key idea is to replace term-level library selection with a typed mechanism grammar, which embeds engineering priors into candidate generation and constrains the search toward physically admissible mechanism compositions. Building on such grammar, we propose Grammar-MD (Grammar-guided Mechanism Discovery), a framework for discovering physically interpretable governing equations in controlled distributed parameter systems. Grammar-MD couples a neural surrogate for derivative estimation, a grammar-guided evolutionary search for mechanism-level candidate generation, and a validation-guided refinement step that identifies a compact active mechanism set. By recovering structured mechanisms rather than trajectory-specific correlations, Grammar-MD is designed to generalize beyond the control inputs used for identification. Experiments on a controlled one-dimensional distributed parameter system demonstrate perfect mechanism-family recovery across a 0%–10% noise sweep, while maintaining reliable term-level identification and coefficient estimation as noise increases. The discovered governing equation also rolls out accurately under unseen control profiles, highlighting the potential of Grammar-MD for interpretable digital twin development.

title: Advanced Supply Chain Planning Under the New Normal: Driving Resilience and Sustainability in a Peruvian Agrifood Company
authors: N. Zacarias; V. Pimentel; D. Huacanca; E. Ramos
source_title: 2026 10th International Conference on Management Engineering, Software Engineering and Service Sciences (ICMSS)
abstract: Agri-food supply chains face mounting pressure from climate variability, market disruptions, and resource scarcity. In this context, advanced planning is key to optimizing operational efficiency and sustainability. Furthermore, strengthening data-driven, digitally supported planning improves coordination and aligns operations with circular and resource-efficient principles. Simultaneously, integrating resilience and sustainability enables adaptive, evidence-based decision-making in the face of uncertainty. This study applies TOPSIS to prioritize the main enablers of advanced planning across technological, operational, and strategic dimensions. Using a Peruvian perishable goods supply chain, the results show that simulation-based hybrid planning delivers better performance, with lower losses, greater resource efficiency, and faster response times. The proposed framework offers practical guidance for resilient and sustainable planning models in emerging economies.

title: Outlining Expectations for Integrating Industry 5.0 Principles into Supply Chain Resilience Strategies
authors: S. Elhidaoui; I. Hakmaoui; R. Elhanna
source_title: 2025 16th International Conference on Logistics and Supply Chain Management (LOGISTIQUA)
abstract: This article explores the integration of Industry 5.0 principles into supply chain resilience strategies, emphasizing the synergy between advanced technologies—such as artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), blockchain, and collaborative robotics—and human-centric, sustainable approaches. Unlike Industry 4.0, which focused on automation and digitalization, Industry 5.0 introduces adaptability, ethical practices, and collaboration as core elements for managing disruptions. The study proposes a strategic framework built on three pillars: human-machine collaboration, sustainability, and predictive resilience, supported by technologies like digital twins, IoT, and blockchain. Real-world case studies in the textile and food industries demonstrate measurable improvements in agility, sustainability, and operational continuity. Despite challenges such as high implementation costs, resistance to change, and the need for specialized skills, Industry 5.0 offers a transformative pathway to building robust, adaptive, and socially responsible supply chains. The article concludes with future research directions, including cross-industry comparisons, regional adaptations, and longitudinal studies to further explore the long-term sustainability of Industry 5.0 integration.

title: Methodology for Designing Embedded Real-Time Electrothermal Models in PYNQ Z1 System on Chip
authors: J. M. Barón; A. Garcia; F. Vergara; P. J. Arnaiz; M. Vasić
abstract: This paper presents a design methodology for Real- Time Digital Twin Electrothermal Models on SoC (Systems on a Chip) developing an analysis of the most relevant constraints for Real-Time Operation and their classification. Moreover, the electrothermal model layout within the architecture of the PYNQ Z1 SoC will be presented exposing the advantages of using an external interface such as Jupyter for Forecasting and the role of parallel structures to accelerate the computation of numerical integration algorithms in Programmable Logic (PL). The proposed electrothermal models will be initially validated with simulation results and later compared with experimental data provided by CMCS (Compact Motor Control System), in which 4 asynchronous engines are supplied by 4 DC/AC IPBB (Inverter Power Building Block).

title: LF-SA Based Solar Cell Parameter Extraction for Floating Photovoltaic Systems
authors: V. Abhinav Kumar; A. Goswami; P. K. Sadhu; S. Bhattacharya
source_title: 2025 International Conference on Power Electronics and Energy (ICPEE)
abstract: The floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems installed in saltwater areas have distinct difficulties with solar cell parameter recovery owing to the corrosive effect of salt-mist, changing temperature, and dynamic operating circumstances that distort IV characteristic. Conventional metaheuristic methods of single-diode model (SDM) fitting can be accused of premature convergence and low accuracy with noisy and time-varying data. In this paper, a hybrid optimization technique combining Levy flight (LF) exploration with Simulated Annealing (SA) exploitation is proposed in order to obtain better accuracy and robustness of the parameter extraction. The LF-SA model is mathematically modeled to fit SDM, tested on artificial and benchmark I-V data, and compared to Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and standalone SA. Findings indicate that there is an increase of $\mathbf{1 5}-\mathbf{2 5 \%}$ in the estimation accuracy and minimized RMSE with no decrease in the computational efficiency that is compatible with embedded monitoring. The method also identifies the indicators of degradation, including resistance building up due to salt intrusion, and assists with predictive maintenance in FPV systems. Such results demonstrate that LF-SA is an encouraging optimization tool towards dependable model of the solar cells and real-time health of offshore PV systems.

title: Feasibility Study of Wireless Sensing with UE-Assisted SAR Imaging Scheme
authors: F. Wang; X. Hou; L. Chen; S. Suyama
abstract: Digital twin technology, envisioned as a cornerstone of sixth-generation (6G) networks, demands robust capabilities for dynamic and real-time environmental reconstruction. Wireless sensing plays a pivotal role in enabling digital twin systems, yet significant challenges persist. High-resolution wireless imaging typically requires large array apertures, which are often accompanied by prohibitive deployment costs and implementation complexity. This paper addresses these limitations by proposing a user equipment (UE)-assisted synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging scheme. The proposed approach exploits UE mobility to emulate a synthetic aperture, enabling high-resolution imaging while reusing existing wireless communication infrastructure. Advanced image reconstruction algorithms, including back projection (BP) and Fourier transform (FT)-based methods, are employed to process echo signals and accurately reconstruct target scenes. To validate the feasibility of the scheme under realistic channel conditions, typical configurations aligned with current network deployments are adopted, and ray-tracing-based channel modeling is applied to representative local areas within urban environments such as Munich and Paris. Preliminary simulation results show that, with a carrier frequency of 3.5 GHz and a bandwidth of 100 MHz, the proposed scheme achieves meter-level resolution in reconstructing building envelopes and capturing distinct structural details. These findings demonstrate the feasibility, scalability, and cost-effectiveness of the UE-assisted SAR imaging framework, paving the way for practical wireless sensing and digital twin applications in future 6 G urban environments.

title: Preliminary Life Cycle Assessment of a HighPerformance Computing Data Center: A Case Study of the HPC4AI Facility at the University of Turin
authors: L. C. Tagliabue; V. Vaccaro; A. Zichi; R. Birke; M. Aldinucci
source_title: 2026 34th Euromicro International Conference on Parallel, Distributed, and Network-Based Processing (PDP)
abstract: High-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) data centers are increasingly recognized as critical infrastructures for scientific research, yet they are also associated with significant environmental burdens due to their high energy intensity and rapid technological obsolescence. Traditional performance metrics such as Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) primarily capture operational efficiency and fail to account for embodied impacts related to construction, equipment manufacturing, and component replacement. This study presents a preliminary Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of the HPC4AI data center at the University of Turin, conducted in accordance with ISO 14040–44 [1] and structured using the EN 15978 modular framework. The assessment adopts a screening-level, attributional LCA with a 30-year reference study period, integrating primary inventory data derived from seven detailed design and equipment schedules covering architectural elements, IT infrastructure, electrical systems, lighting, and cooling equipment. Life-cycle impacts are quantified for the modules A1–A3 (product stage), B4 (replacement due to technological obsolescence), and B6 (operational energy use), while other modules are structurally included as placeholders. Global warming potential (GWP) is used as the impact indicator, with multiple electricity mix scenarios applied to evaluate operational sensitivity. Results indicate that operational electricity use (Module B6) is the dominant contributor to life-cycle GWP, confirming findings from recent HPC and AI data center LCAs. However, embodied impacts associated with IT and cooling equipment manufacturing and replacement (A1–A3 + B4) represent a substantial secondary contribution, with replacement impacts of comparable magnitude to initial construction. A component-level ranking reveals that servers, UPS systems, and core cooling equipment are the principal sources of embodied emissions, while architectural components contribute marginally. The study highlights the critical role of electricity decarbonization, hardware lifetime management, and circular strategies in reducing the environmental footprint of academic HPC facilities. Despite its screening nature, the LCA provides a robust baseline for future refined assessments and supports the integration of life-cycle thinking into the design and governance of research-oriented data centers.

title: Smart Technologies and the Resilience of Sustainable Supply Chains: A Systematic Review Following PRISMA Guidelines
authors: A. Diani; L. Aligod
source_title: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Technologies in Supply Chain Management (ATSCM)
abstract: Supply chains have undergone several changes resulting from environmental uncertainty, which pushes every company wishing to be competitive to seek resilience and sustainability as two essential strategic axes. Smart technologies offer new opportunities to address disruptions and optimize performance. This article examines emerging technologies for resilience, sustainability, and emerging digital technologies. The authors conduct a systematic review of 41 peer-reviewed articles from 2015 to 2025 to present a comprehensive overview of current trends. This research aims to analyze five main themes: visibility and traceability; predictive decision-making; scenario planning; automation and production flexibility; integration into a digital ecosystem. The more established technologies primarily improve detection, preparedness, and response. However, the technologies analyzed play an essential role in recovery and adaptation. The social dimension of sustainability also remains understudied. By consolidating more fragmented research, the authors develop an integrative framework that provides guidance for future studies in the areas of advanced technologies, long-term resilience, and social inclusion.

title: 13 MIND-SHIELD: A Multi-Intelligence Deep Learning Framework for Hierarchical Threat Detection and Zero-shot Situational Intelligence Process
abstract: This book provides a comprehensive exploration of how artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing cyber risk management, offering advanced methodologies to identify, assess, quantify, and mitigate threats effectively. Through the integration of AI, big data analytics, and emerging technologies, this book presents cutting-edge approaches to addressing cyber risks. Readers will gain insights into how AI enhances threat detection, fraud prevention, risk quantification, and incident response, equipping businesses to anticipate, measure, and mitigate cyber disruptions with greater precision. In today’s digital landscape, businesses increasingly depend on complex cyber systems including cloud computing and data infrastructure, enterprise systems, financial and payment, and other operational systems, which make them susceptible to a wide range of risks beyond conventional security threats. Downtimes, system failures, data breaches, and cyber infrastructure outages can cause significant operational, reputational, and financial disruptions. To navigate these challenges, organizations must move beyond traditional risk management approaches and adopt AI-driven solutions for more proactive and intelligent cyber risk management. Structured around key aspects of AI-driven cyber risk management, the book begins with foundational principles before delving into the rise of AI in cyber risk management, the role of big data in risk analysis, and the application of AI in threat intelligence and fraud detection. Readers will explore AI-powered risk quantification models, automated mitigation strategies, and the integration of AI into cybersecurity infrastructure, business continuity planning, and disaster recovery. Industry-specific case studies offer real-world insights into AI’s impact across different sectors, while discussions on emerging technologies, such as IoT, blockchain, large language models, advanced machine learning, and explainable AI, highlight the future trajectory of AI in cyber risk management. Aimed at professionals, researchers, and students, this book balances technical depth with practical clarity, making it an essential guide for those seeking to bridge the gap between AI innovation and real-world cyber risk applications. By addressing both the potential and challenges of AI-driven solutions, it presents a forward-thinking strategy for building resilient, AI-powered cyber risk management frameworks.
